stem.en: Silver sits below copper on the ladder. Kabir puts a silver spoon and a copper coin in nimbu and reads the meter. Which way do the electrons flow, and about how many volts?

text.en: From copper to silver, through the wire. Copper is higher, so it gives. The gap is small, about half a volt.

feedback.en: Precious means it holds its electrons, which is why it does not tarnish easily. Holding tight is low on the ladder, not high.

text.en: No flow; both are shiny metals.

feedback.en: Any two different rungs give a push. Only the same metal on both sides gives zero.

text.en: From copper to silver, at 3 volts.

feedback.en: Volts are the gap between rungs, and copper and silver are close neighbours. Magnesium against silver would be big. Copper against silver is small.

explanation.en: Find both metals on the ladder. The higher one gives. The gap is the volts.
